title: Family honors 17-year-old Ashton Kepler with memorial parking spot in Newark
text:
A parking spot is something most people probably never think twice about, but for Ashton Kepler's family, it is now a place to remember a 17-year-old they say is impossible to forget.
Friends and family paint a parking spot in memory of 17-year-old Ashton Kepler in Newark on Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. Kepler was killed in a motorcycle crash three days earlier.
Newark, N.Y. — A parking spot is something most people probably never think twice about, but for Ashton Kepler's family, it is now a place to remember a 17-year-old they say is impossible to forget.
"He was definitely the one to meet and the one to know, because he was the brightest light you will ever see," said Ashton's mother, Carla Kepler. Ashton worked at Canal View Family Restaurant in Newark. His family said he loved working, playing sports and spending time with the people he loved. Carla said she and Ashton shared a love of the Buffalo Bills and enjoyed traveling together.
They had already started planning their next trip.
"He was going into the Marines, and before he got stationed, he wanted to go on one last trip with me," Carla said. Ashton was killed in a motorcycle crash early Sunday on Wood Lane in Arcadia, according to New York State Police. His motorcycle went off the road and entered a ditch around 12:25 a.m. First responders took him to Newark-Wayne Community Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
